If the lock cannot be taken, the run appends one refusal line to the set's backup log (appending, never truncating, because the log belongs to the live holder), marks the set failed and returns. The prior-state reads (the last backup time, the guard against a populated index with no last backup time, and the witness gate) keep their order and run under a guard that releases the lock and re-raises the ORIGINAL error, so the witness refusal still maps to exit 3 and the backup log is left as the last run wrote it. Creating the run log is guarded the same way. Staging setup receives the held lock and passes it to reclaim, which only logs that a current-version holder is excluded and that an older FileBackup takes no OS lock; classification, the confirmation sample and the refusals are untouched (SR-086). If staging setup fails, the lock is released first. Otherwise the lock is released in the run's final cleanup, after the heartbeat is stopped and in a way that cannot be skipped; on the healthy path that is after the snapshot is published, run state is written, deduplication and the browse view run, and it also runs on every error and every lock-lost return. Test seams sit right after the marker is deleted and on either side of the snapshot-publishing rename.

design.Title: Prune holds the same OS lock
design.Detail: Prune takes the staging OS lock once, after resolving the roots and before working through the named snapshots, and so before committed-residue removal, the rails, the staging-area creation and every re-home, unless -WhatIf is in effect. If the lock cannot be taken, prune reports every named snapshot as Status Refused, Code 4 (retry later, as a backup; Get-StoreRefusalCode), with a single refusal of kind lock-held whose message is the [SR-075/lock-held] text, and returns. The lock is held for the whole batch and released in prune's final cleanup. The existing staging-area rail, the create-without-overwrite staging take and PRUNE.inprogress are unchanged. A test seam runs right after PRUNE.inprogress is written.

design.Title: Lock file lifecycle and invisibility
design.Detail: Nothing deletes, writes or truncates Temp.lock. Every enumeration of the change root lists directories only (the engine's snapshot inventory additionally filters by the snapshot pattern, and every prune, audit, kit-refresh and -Action Snapshots path reaches the change root through it; both restorers build their pool from directories), so the lock file is invisible to all of them. Committed prune residue and the staging area are addressed by exact name.

design.Title: Repair and kit refresh hold the same OS lock
design.Detail: Storage-form repair and the kit refresh hold the same staging OS lock. Taking it for them refuses a blank change root, creates a missing one, and then takes the OS lock; on any failure it logs one ERROR line through the caller's logger and refuses with a message carrying [SR-075/lock-held]. Repair takes it as its FIRST act, before the storage-form audit, so findings and repair see one state; the kit refresh takes it before listing the snapshots. Both skip it under -WhatIf, and both release it in a final cleanup around their whole body. The lock lives in the mutating operations, not in the verify entry point, so a direct module caller is covered; the verify entry point turns the refusal into exit code 2. A read-only -Action Verify runs only the storage-form audit and the pool-resolution check and takes no lock. Left lock-free because they do not write the store: -Action Snapshots, -Action View (it writes only the view root, which the SR-063 rails keep outside both roots), the -Deep audit (its scratch files are under the system temporary directory) and both restorers (they write only the restore target). Every other engine step that writes the store is a backup or prune step reached only from a backup run or a prune; several of those steps can also be called directly as module exports, and such a direct caller holds no lock.

design.Title: One store folder per backup set (plan C44)
design.Detail: A backup set names one StorePath (ConfigVersion 3); BackupPath and ChangePath are refused by name in JSON and CLIXML, and versions 1 and 2 as too old. The loader derives the latest state as <StorePath>/CurrentBackup and the change root as <StorePath>, and the snapshots sit in <StorePath>/BackupHistory, with path arithmetic that needs no attached drive, so an unplugged store drive still reports 4 (C25). Path resolution creates a missing store, its BackupHistory and then its CurrentBackup only when safe: a store holding a MANIFEST.csv of its own, a folder beside CurrentBackup holding one other than the store's own View, Verify, Incoming and Temp folders, or a folder of old Snapshot_<date> folders, is an old-layout backup and is refused (2); a store holding snapshots but no CurrentBackup is refused (2), never answered with a fresh full backup; a store with a CurrentBackup but no BackupHistory is refused (2) for every action, with a message saying an empty BackupHistory folder lets the run go on, and BackupHistory is never created for an existing store. CurrentBackup, BackupHistory and the store must be one volume and one mount, proven by test renames. The browse view defaults to <StorePath>/View and may lie inside the store only there.

design.Title: Shard folders of the latest state (plan C44, L8)
design.Detail: An object of the latest state lives at CurrentBackup/<xx>/<name>, xx being the first two characters of its name lowercased (the folder pattern ^[2-9a-z]{2}$, 'l' included); snapshots stay flat and a DataPath stays the bare name. One Common function gives an object's path from its state folder, its name and whether that folder is the latest state; the caller says which, nothing infers it from a folder's name. Listing the latest state reads a file only from its own shard folder, so the run's index, retention, the audit and both restorers' name indexes agree that a file anywhere else in CurrentBackup is no object. -Action Verify reports such a file as MisplacedObject and -RepairStorage moves it into Verify/. The shard folder is created before the rename that publishes an object into it; an emptied one is left in place.

design.Title: '/' as the only recorded separator (plan C44, L7)
design.Detail: The source walk converts every relative path to '/' once, so MANIFEST.csv and DIRECTORIES.csv record the same RelativePath on every host and every later comparison (change detection, the unreadable-folder prefixes, case-only collisions, the directory record's ancestors) sees one form. On Windows '\' becomes '/'; on Linux a '\' is part of a name, which SR-055 refuses as unportable, so it is never recorded. The restorers keep mapping a '\' to '/' on a POSIX host for a manifest an older engine wrote.

design.Title: Restore kit revision 16: the store is found from the kit's own folder (plan C44, S3, L9)
design.Detail: Both restorers run from a folder named exactly CurrentBackup, whose parent is the store, or a dated folder whose parent is named BackupHistory, whose grandparent is the store; a dated folder anywhere else is no snapshot. The pool is <store>/CurrentBackup plus every dated folder in <store>/BackupHistory, and a restore from CurrentBackup still runs with BackupHistory missing, reporting a row whose object was in a snapshot as missing (1). No path sidecar is written or read and no sibling or child folder is guessed. From any other folder a restorer refuses with 2 before writing anything, unless -StoreRootOverride / --store-root names the store. The target must be outside the store and outside the restore's own origin folder. The kit has six files.

Prune's own staging-busy refusal and its marker are unchanged, so this is also the SR-046 mutual-exclusion regression (invariant I-3).

test.Parameters: Two runs started concurrently against one stale marker-only Temp, released together at the classification barrier so both reach the Directory.Move.
test.Expected: Exactly one proceeds; the loser fails the move (or the subsequent New-Item) and refuses without retrying in a loop. Afterwards exactly one Temp exists and its RUN.inprogress carries the WINNER's RunId, and no aside folder survives holding anything but a marker. A DETERMINISTIC INTERLEAVING is also required (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-3): reclaimer B stalled at a test seam between its confirmation sample and its move while reclaimer A completes its whole reclaim, so B's move takes A's freshly recreated LIVE Temp -- B must detect the identity mismatch after the move, move the folder straight BACK and refuse, leaving A's marker intact at the original path and no aside folder behind. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the atomic move replaced by a delete-then-create, or the step-3 New-Item given -Force, this case must be shown to FAIL (both proceed, or the marker is the loser's). Invariant I-2.

test.Parameters: An EMPTY Temp with no marker, run twice: once with the directory's own mtime aged past the threshold (a pre-WP14 store, which is literally the hub's state) and once with it freshly created (a live run inside its create-to-marker window).
test.Expected: Stale directory mtime is reclaimed and the run completes, so the upgrade path from a pre-WP14 store costs nothing; fresh directory mtime is REFUSED, which is the gate that stops a reclaimer stealing a live lock in the microseconds between New-Item and the marker publish.

test.Parameters: A RUN.inprogress whose mtime is set into the future relative to the reader, at offsets both inside and far beyond the threshold, fed through Read-StagingOwnerRecord and Get-StagingLockState.
test.Expected: Classified OwnerLive and refused. Clock skew is handled conservatively in the harmless direction: a future mtime can only be a clock disagreement, never proof of death.

test.Parameters: The G8 real-volume suite on Windows against an actual exFAT-formatted volume: a stale marker-only Temp reclaimed end to end, plus an ambiguous Directory.Move failure injected on the same volume.
test.Expected: The reclaim completes on exFAT with the aside folder removed and the run at exit 0, and the injected move failure REFUSES with both paths untouched and no writer started -- never a fallback to delete. Half of the plan's Q1 evidence: .NET does not promise rename atomicity, so the supported-provider list is defined from this evidence.

test.Parameters: Container acceptance inside filebackup:local on the deployment's Linux-over-exFAT bind mount: the same stale-marker reclaim, with the boot id read from /proc and the host and container id recorded in the marker.
test.Expected: The reclaim completes inside the container and the run reaches exit 0; the record's diagnostic identity fields are populated from the container's own view. This is the deployment the defect was actually found in, and the other half of Q1 -- one Windows run is not evidence for this stack.

test.Parameters: The existing TC-073 staging-cleanup case and the four catch cleanups re-run unchanged, plus an exception injected at each major phase AFTER staging has gained content.
test.Expected: TC-073 and the four catch cleanups remain green, and in every injected-exception case the heartbeat is stopped and drained by the Part B finally -- no live timer is left advertising an abandoned lock as owned, and the successor run therefore classifies it OwnerStale rather than OwnerLive. The catch blocks alone cover only the early exits, which is the regression risk this case exists for.

test.Parameters: Run A paused by a test hook AFTER its New-Item of Temp and BEFORE the marker publish; run B meanwhile classifies the empty directory per TC-192 and reclaims it; run A is then released.
test.Expected: A's exclusive FileMode.CreateNew publish FAILS because RUN.inprogress now exists (B's), and A aborts immediately, touching nothing -- no move, no delete, no change folder, and NOTHING left in B's Temp, which holds its own RUN.inprogress and nothing else (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-4: the old temp-write publish could strand a '.tmp' in a folder A no longer owned, itself a permanent wedge) -- logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the publish made non-exclusive (a create-or-truncate write) this case must be shown to FAIL, with A silently continuing to write into B's staging folder. The window is microseconds wide; correctness must not depend on that.

test.Parameters: A reclaim whose test hook drops a data file into the ASIDE folder between the step-4 re-enumeration and the delete -- the last window in the protocol.
test.Expected: The exact-leaf marker delete may succeed, but the non-recursive Directory.Delete then FAILS because the directory is not empty; the aside folder is kept with the injected bytes intact, the failure is logged loudly with the README recovery, and the run continues. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with a recursive delete restored in place of the non-recursive one, this case must be shown to FAIL by destroying the injected file. This race is the entire reason -Recurse is banned from the reclaim path.

test.Parameters: Read-StagingOwnerRecord and Get-StagingLockState against a truncated marker, a marker of unknown SchemaVersion, a marker whose StaleAfterSeconds is BELOW 1800 s, and a marker held open with a deny-read lock or an ACL that blocks reading -- each at both stale and fresh mtimes.
test.Expected: Truncated and unknown-schema markers return ParseInvalid with LastWriteUtc and AgeSeconds populated and fall back to mtime alone with the 1800 s reader floor applied (a below-floor StaleAfterSeconds cannot shorten it), reclaiming when stale and refusing when fresh; ParseInvalid is never an error, because a torn record is precisely a writer that died mid-publish and refusing it would recreate the permanent wedge for the commonest crash. The unreadable marker returns Unreadable and REFUSES: absence of evidence is not evidence of death.

test.Parameters: Get-StagingLockState fed enumerations containing hidden, system and dot-named entries; an enumeration that raises an I/O or access error; and a Temp that is a symlink/junction to another tree.
test.Expected: Hidden, system and dot-named entries all classify HoldsContent -- forced enumeration means they are content like any other. An enumeration, stat or access failure classifies Indeterminate and refuses: an I/O error is never evidence of emptiness. A reparse-point Temp is refused outright, because moving or deleting through one acts on a tree the guard never classified.

test.Parameters: A heartbeat callback deliberately held in flight (a test seam blocking inside the touch) across a Stop-StagingHeartbeat call, while a successor acquires Temp and publishes a marker with a DIFFERENT RunId; the held callback is then released.
test.Expected: Stop blocks until the in-flight callback drains, and the released callback finds a RunId that is not its own and does not touch: the successor's marker mtime is NOT freshened, so the successor's own staleness is judged on its own beat. Stop is also idempotent when called twice. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with either layer removed -- the drain or the RunId identity guard -- this case must be shown to FAIL by freshening the successor's marker.

test.Parameters: A full changed-run finalize through Complete-ChangeFolder, plus the no-op and first-run paths, each starting from a staging lock that carried a RUN.inprogress; the produced dated snapshot is then pruned.
test.Expected: No RUN.inprogress exists anywhere inside the produced dated snapshot on any of the three paths -- the marker is stopped, drained and deleted as a leaf immediately before finalize -- and that snapshot prunes WITHOUT an unreferenced-data refusal. Left in place, the marker would be renamed wholesale into every snapshot and then refused by SR-046's rail as a file its manifest does not name.

test.Parameters: The writer's clock set BEHIND the reader's by more than StaleAfterSeconds (the marker therefore reads as long stale on first sample) while the owner is genuinely alive and beating; the reader then takes its confirmation sample.
test.Expected: The confirmation sample sees the mtime MOVE, so the owner is judged live and the run is refused with [SR-075/owner-live] -- no clock configuration can cause a live owner to be stomped, because the second sample is clock-free. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the confirmation sample removed (age alone deciding), this case must be shown to FAIL by reclaiming a live owner's lock. This is the skew direction the first draft had backwards.

test.Parameters: A test hook that swaps Temp's RUN.inprogress for one carrying a different RunId, applied at each of the FIVE fence points in turn: before the step-7 staging manifest write, before Move-RemovedFilesToStaging, before Save-SupersededData, before the backup-root MANIFEST.csv publish and before Complete-ChangeFolder (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-2/R-10).
test.Expected: At every fence the run aborts BEFORE that phase mutates the pool or publishes state, cleans up NOTHING (the folder is no longer its own to delete), and logs [SR-075/lock-lost]. Per fence: no stored data byte ceases to exist anywhere in the store, the snapshot set and FileBackupState.json are unchanged, and MANIFEST.csv and its DIRECTORIES.csv sidecar are unchanged at every fence that precedes the backup-root publish. At the finalize fence -- the only one that FOLLOWS that publish, the run having still owned the lock one step earlier -- the manifest is this run's own canonical step-12 output and nothing was finalized over it. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the fence check removed at each point IN TURN, this case must be shown to FAIL -- the run proceeds past that boundary, finalizes a snapshot, deletes the successor's owner record and publishes state.

test.Parameters: Every extension WP17 Part A appends to $script:NonCompressibleExtensions - .z7 .esd .mpg .mpeg .m2ts .m4v .wmv .flv .heic .heif .opus .m4a - in lower, upper and mixed case; plus the deliberate NON-additions .iso .mca .bin .dng .pdf.

test.Parameters: Measure-SampleCompressibility called directly via InModuleScope over synthetic corpora BUILT IN THE TEST: pure random bytes; repeated text; a random file with a 64 KiB text head; a file one third text; a 500 KiB file; a 4 KiB file; an empty file; a vanished path; and a path held open with FileShare.None. Constants read through InModuleScope ($script:CompressProbeThreshold 0.10, $script:CompressProbeMinBytes 262144).
test.Expected: Aggregate CompressedBytes/SampledBytes is approximately 1.0 for random, far below 1 for text, approximately 0.93 for the mixed-head file (so the aggregate rule keeps it RAW where an any-sample rule would have compressed it - the defect review's own failure mode) and approximately 0.7 for the mixed-third file (so it COMPRESSES). The 500 KiB file is below Samples x SampleBytes and is therefore read exactly ONCE as a single whole-file sample, not as three overlapping windows. The vanished path and the FileShare.None-locked path each return $null rather than throwing. Random bytes must NOT measure below 0.98, which is the assertion that pins the compressed count being taken AFTER Dispose() - a count read before the encoder is closed reads short and would call random bytes compressible. Offsets are 0, floor((len - SampleBytes)/2) and len - SampleBytes, and the open uses FileShare.Read.

test.Parameters: A full backup run per arm, mode always and then mode off, above the 256 KiB floor: a .docx whose bytes are random, a .jpg whose bytes are text, and a .txt. The Owner's Q7 ruling under test.

Filename extension and the Compressed column agree in all six arms.

test.Parameters: Mode always, every file above the 256 KiB floor: an unlisted extension and a no-extension file over each of random, text, mixed-head and mixed-third content; plus a LISTED .zip over text and the same .zip over random.
test.Expected: Random stores raw, text stores .7z, mixed-head (aggregate ~0.93) stores RAW, mixed-third (aggregate ~0.7) stores .7z; the listed .zip over text stores .7z and over random stores raw - the defining property of the default mode, that the list is not consulted above the floor. In every arm the stored filename's extension and the row's Compressed column agree (SR-004's agreement sentence, I-1). NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: with the probe BYPASSED so the decision falls back to the extension list, this case must be shown to FAIL - the random arms compress.

test.Parameters: Invoke-BackupFileGroup called DIRECTLY in-process (the suites drive backups through FileBackup.ps1, which re-imports both modules with -Force at FileBackup.ps1:236 and thereby discards any Mock -ModuleName injected earlier; Mock -ModuleName FileBackup.Engine on a direct call has precedent at Coverage.Tests.ps1:1862), with Measure-SampleCompressibility mocked behind a call counter. test.Parameters: CompressProbe across both configuration formats, driven from the ONE shared fixture corpus tests/Common/ConfigFixtures.ps1. Each of "Always", "maybe", null and a number aborts with exit 2 NAMING the key, creating nothing, in JSON AND in CLIXML - the CLIXML arms are what prove the value check lives in Test-BackupConfigurationShape beside the BrowseView block (-cnotin) and not only in the JSON-only closed key set. The published container/FileBackup.schema.json enum equals the validator's vocabulary (TC-077 parity). test.Parameters: Invoke-BackupFileGroup called DIRECTLY, mode always, a file above the 256 KiB floor, in TWO arms. (A) The probe is unavailable for every candidate (Measure-SampleCompressibility yields no measurement) while the bytes stay READABLE, so the copy itself succeeds. (B) A REAL FileShare.None handle is held on EVERY member of the group, so no candidate can be opened by the probe - nor by the copy, which is why the two arms are separate.
test.Expected: Both arms: the decision is ProbeUnavailable and its Compress value is THE LIST'S ANSWER - today's behaviour, not a default of 'compress' - with EXACTLY ONE WARN over the whole group (the group-scope memo, LLR-058) and exactly one 'compress-decision: <rel> ProbeUnavailable' DEBUG line. No probe error propagates and the destination is never opened. Arm A additionally: the object IS written and the run stays successful - fail-toward-today, never fail-the-run: a lock costs a decision, never a file (I-6). Arm B additionally: the ONLY failure is SR-067's ordinary copy failure on the locked source (the copy cannot read a file the probe cannot read either), so nothing about that failure is attributable to the probe.

test.Parameters: -Action Verify over a probe-MIXED store (objects in both storage forms, some raw-stored with archive-magic bytes under their own .z7 name) using TC-093's harness, non-Deep and then -Deep, with Get-FileXxHash mocked behind a call counter. Then a full restore of the same store by Reconstruct.ps1 and by bash/reconstruct.sh.
test.Expected: The audit reports CLEAN over the probe-mixed store - both forms are still just forms. A raw-stored .z7 (Compressed=No over 7-Zip magic) whose DataPath extension equals the row's RelativePath extension and whose on-disk length equals the row's Length is EXEMPTED WITHOUT A HASH: the mocked Get-FileXxHash counter is 0 on the non-Deep scan and greater than 0 under -Deep, where the confirming hash is retained. Reconstruct.ps1 and reconstruct.sh each reproduce every object BYTE-EXACT from the mixed store.

test.Parameters: TC-225's arms re-run INSIDE the filebackup:local container image on the Linux stack, mode always, with the set summary captured.

The summary REPORTS the 'Probe reads: <bytes>' counter and the wall time the probe cost, so the first-run cost claim is MEASURED rather than asserted; the figures are recorded, and no pass budget is set until there is production data to set one from (no PB row is invented here).

test.Parameters: Arm 1 (rule 0): CompressEnabled=false, every mode (off, excluded-extensions, always) x every extension class (SN-003's example names, listed, unlisted, none), above and below the floor, with Measure-SampleCompressibility mocked behind a call counter. Arm 2 (Part A end to end): a .z7 source under CompressEnabled=true, mode off, with Compress-FileWithSevenZip mocked behind a call counter.
test.Expected: Arm 1: every file is stored RAW with Compressed=No, the probe call counter is 0 (no probe is opened, no 7-Zip is resolved), and a Plain set never names an object .7z. Arm 2: the .z7 source is stored raw and the Compress-FileWithSevenZip counter is 0 - 7z is not invoked at all - which is the hub's actual fix path and the nine days Part A recovers. test.Parameters: FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL over Compress-FileWithSevenZip and over the FileBackup.ps1 startup path. The 7-Zip invocation is captured by passing -SevenZipPath a fake 7z .cmd that writes its own argument line to a file (the function takes the executable as a parameter, so no seam is needed), run in a CHILD pwsh per arm because the level is resolved at Common's import. Windows-only arms (the fake 7z is a cmd script and the entry-point arms run on Windows); Linux/container behavioural coverage of the knob is a recorded gap.
test.Expected: (a) the argument list carries -mx=9 - the pre-existing behaviour is exactly the default; (b) -mx=1; (c) -mx=0 and -mx=9 are accepted, so the whole 0-9 range is usable; (d) every invalid value, the lookalikes included, leaves Import-Module FileBackup.Common succeeding in a child pwsh with NO throw, (Get-FileBackupDefaults).SevenZipCompressionLevel = 9 and the raw value recorded as rejected, and the kit-shaped load path exits 0 the same way (the lookalikes passed the original culture-sensitive membership gate, so the [int] cast threw AT IMPORT - inside a restore kit, over a backup-only setting; 2026-09-01 dual review R-1); (e) a compression-enabled backup refuses before it creates anything - exit 2, the SR-042/SR-043 usage/precondition code under -ExitCode and a terminating error without it, no new code - with stderr naming FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL, the 0-9 range, the rejected value's length and every non-printable character escaped as \uXXXX, and no backup root, change root or log created; (f) the same class of invalid value leaves the Plain control run completing normally (exit 0, files stored); (g) the real 7-Zip round trip returns byte-identical content at both levels and the stored object carries the 7-Zip signature - the arm that earns the claim that any level's archive restores with the same kit; (h) neither restorer makes a DIRECT reference to FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL. The restorers read no POLICY from the variable and restore correctness is level-independent; Reconstruct.ps1's host self-test does compress its own throwaway probe file, so that probe archive inherits the resolved level, which is harmless because every 0-9 archive round-trips (pinned by (g)).

test.Parameters: Second run with HashRecalcFreq=A (recalc always due); Optimize-ChangeFolders mocked to throw at step 15 (stand-in for a SIGKILL in dedupe).
test.Expected: Run state is persisted before the cross-change dedupe (defect review M-4): after a run that dies in step 15, the step-13 snapshot of the prior state is published and LastBackupRun and LastHashRun both equal this run's date, so the next snapshot is not named stale and the weekly rehash does not repeat nightly. Get-BackupContentIndex default call; retained managed bytes after a full collection, measured with GC.GetTotalMemory(true) with the result held live. tests/Unit/ManifestAtomicWrite.Tests.ps1, Describe 'Write-Manifest publishes MANIFEST.csv atomically'. A folder is seeded with the OLD complete manifest; Write-Manifest(NEW) is interrupted by the ManifestWriteTestHook seam throwing at each boundary (after truncating the staging file to half or zero where the case says so). The SHA-256 of MANIFEST.csv is IN {old, new} at every kill point (and so never zero-length or truncated), equals OLD before the rename and NEW after it; a kill after the rename leaves a witness that mismatches; a relative folder lands in the PowerShell location, not the process directory; a failing rename removes the staging file and leaves the destination alone; an empty record set still writes and verifies. MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-10-09: writing MANIFEST.csv in place again fails the single BeIn assertion at ManifestAtomicWrite.Tests.ps1:115 for the torn-at-half and zero-length cases.

tests/Unit/ManifestAtomicWrite.Tests.ps1, Describe 'A process killed at each Write-Manifest boundary never tears MANIFEST.csv'. A child pwsh runs Write-Manifest(NEW) over a seeded folder with a hook that parks it (writes a flag file, sleeps 600 s) at the stage, truncating the staging file first in the torn case; the parent waits for the flag and then Stop-Process -Force (TerminateProcess / SIGKILL), so no finally, catch or flush in the child can run. SCOPE: a real process kill at each of three boundaries, with tearing SIMULATED by truncating the already-complete temp file before parking; the Export-Csv interval itself is never killed mid-write. The SHA-256 of MANIFEST.csv is IN {old, new}. Mutation-checked with TC-237 (fails at :228 for the torn case).

tests/Unit/ManifestAtomicWrite.Tests.ps1 Describe 'A leftover MANIFEST.csv.tmp breaks nothing' and tests/Unit/StagingLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'The Write-Manifest staging file in Temp is not content'. The next Write-Manifest over each kind of leftover publishes the complete NEW file (hash) and consumes the temp file, with a verified witness; Get-DataFile returns the nested sub\MANIFEST.csv.tmp and not the root one; Test-BackupManifest raises no orphan WARN; Test-BackupStorageForm raises no finding in the root or a snapshot; Get-StagingLockState gives OwnerStale for a stale marker plus the staging file, OwnerLive for a fresh one, HoldsContent when a MANIFEST.csv or a case-differing name is also there; a real stale Temp holding the marker and the staging file is reclaimed with the aside folder removed, one that also holds a data file is refused with every hash unchanged, and a run that fails early with the staging file in its own Temp removes that Temp. Mutation-checked: dropping the allowlist entry fails 4 tests; dropping the classifier filter fails 4; removing the by-name temp delete in Clear-ReclaimedStagingFolder fails only the aside-folder-GONE assertion (StagingLock.Tests.ps1:2080).

tests/Unit/ManifestAtomicWrite.Tests.ps1 Describe 'A leftover MANIFEST.csv.tmp through whole backup runs'. Three real Invoke-BackupSet runs over a source holding a nested user file sub\MANIFEST.csv.tmp, with a torn MANIFEST.csv.tmp planted in the backup root before runs 2 and 3 and in the snapshot before run 3. All three runs succeed; backup.log has no WARN naming the leftover; the manifest has no row for the root-level file and exactly one for the nested user file (B6); the root leftover is consumed; the witness verifies.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'The staging OS lock primitive'. Get-StagingOsLockPath is <ChangeRoot>/Temp.lock; a second Enter-StagingOsLock while the first is held throws a message carrying [SR-075/lock-held]; after Exit the lock can be taken again; Exit is idempotent and accepts $null; the file is still there, zero-length, after release; on Windows it cannot be deleted while held; a read-only attribute on it does not stop the lock being taken.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'The lock is released on every way a run ends in-process'. Four in-process Invoke-BackupSet runs end normally, by a mocked Save-SupersededData throw (rethrown), by a content-holding Temp refusal, and by a marker swapped at a RunId fence; after each, this process can take the change root's OS lock.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'A hard kill releases the lock'. A child pwsh running a real backup is parked at StagingTestHook_AfterMarkerDelete; while parked the parent cannot take the lock; after Stop-Process -Force (TerminateProcess) it can. SCOPE: Windows only; SIGKILL on Linux is the same claim by the same mechanism and is not run here.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'The lock is held across the whole no-marker window' (design E3). A child pwsh runs a real third backup (one file changed, one removed, so Temp holds evicted and superseded bytes) and is parked at each end of the window, where Temp exists and holds no RUN.inprogress. At each point: the parent cannot take the lock; a concurrent backup fails its set with [SR-075/lock-held] in backup.log; a concurrent prune of the existing snapshot is refused with [SR-075/lock-held] in its message; and the SHA-256 of every file under BackupPath and ChangePath is unchanged after each contender (backup.log excluded: the refusal must be logged; the held lock file recorded by length). MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-10-09: releasing the OS lock just before the RUN.inprogress delete fails the single assertion StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1:428 (BackupLog Should -Match lock-held) at both window points -- the contender then took the lock and was refused only by the content rule ([SR-075/content-refused]) -- and also :423 and the prune-token assertion; the byte assertion :438 still PASSES under that mutation, because today's content refusal is the second wall the coming recovery will remove.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'Prune against a live backup past its finalize rename'. A child backup is parked at StagingTestHook_AfterFinalizeRename, where Temp has already been renamed into the new snapshot and Optimize-ChangeFolders is next. A prune of the older snapshot is Refused with code 4 (retry later, as a backup; kind lock-held; code 2 until 2026-10-27) and [SR-075/lock-held], and the SHA-256 of every file under BackupPath and ChangePath is unchanged. MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-10-09: with Remove-BackupSnapshot skipping the lock, the prune REMOVED the snapshot under the live backup, failing the single byte assertion StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1:478 (and the code-2 and token assertions).

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'Backup against a live prune'. A child Remove-BackupSnapshot is parked at PruneTestHook_InTransaction (Temp and PRUNE.inprogress present, lock held). A backup fails its set with [SR-075/lock-held] and the SHA-256 of every file under BackupPath and ChangePath, the prune's Temp included, is unchanged.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'Reclaim against a live run whose marker looks dead'. A frozen run is modelled by a child that only holds the OS lock while Temp carries a marker three hours stale and unchanging -- a folder the SR-075 rules alone reclaim. With the confirmation sample compressed, the backup refuses with [SR-075/lock-held], moves nothing aside and changes no byte. Control arm: with the holder killed, the same backup over the same folder logs [SR-075/reclaimed], proving the lock was the only thing that refused.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'A free lock is not proof of death'. An older FileBackup's live run is represented by a Temp with a FRESH RUN.inprogress and no OS lock held. The lock is free (precondition), the backup acquires it, and still refuses [SR-075/owner-live] and fails the set with every byte unchanged; a stale marker plus a data file still refuses [SR-075/content-refused] unchanged. MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-10-09: with Invoke-StagingLockReclaim treating its acquired -OsLock as proof of death, the run reclaimed the live Temp and completed, failing the single byte assertion StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1:618 (and the owner-live, set-failed and content assertions).

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'An open failure that is not a sharing violation is LIVE'. Each arm makes the lock-file open fail -- a real directory squatting on Temp.lock, or the StagingOsLockTestHook_BeforeOpen seam throwing -- over a store whose Temp is reclaimable, so proceeding would be visible. The backup logs [SR-075/lock-held], the prune is Refused with code 4, as the backup (2 until 2026-10-27), and the SHA-256 of every file under BackupPath and ChangePath, the reclaimable Temp included, is unchanged.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describes 'The lock file is invisible to every consumer of the store' and 'Where the lock is taken and released, statically'. After three runs Temp.lock is at the change root with length 0; with it HELD, the snapshot list is exactly the dated snapshot folders, the storage-form audit and pool resolution report nothing, Optimize-ChangeFolders runs, the latest state restores byte-exact against the source and every snapshot restores. From the engine AST: Initialize-StagingFolder's only caller is Invoke-BackupSet; Enter-StagingOsLock precedes it there; Invoke-BackupSet's four Exit-StagingOsLock calls are in the step-2.95, logger and step-3 catches and after Complete-ChangeFolder; no Get-LastBackupRun, Get-LastHashRun, Read-Manifest, Test-ManifestWitness or Test-Path call in Invoke-BackupSet precedes its Enter-StagingOsLock; Remove-BackupSnapshot's Enter-StagingOsLock precedes Remove-CommittedPruneResidue. Describe 'A run reads the prior store state only after it holds the lock' (added 2026-10-10 after review): run A, the store's FIRST backup, is a child pwsh parked holding the lock at its first fence (before any manifest or LastBackupRun exists); run B starts, and its StagingOsLockTestHook_BeforeOpen seam lets A run to completion and waits for it to exit (exit 0, precondition) before B's open; only then is a.txt changed. B completes, the SHA-256 of A's stored a.txt is still present under BackupPath or ChangePath, and the only snapshot is the one named by A's date. MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-10-10: with the LastBackupRun read and the no-LastBackupRun guard moved back above the lock, B took itself for a first backup and completed while discarding A's version -- failing the single assertion StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1:1102 (A's bytes present) and the snapshot assertion; B still reported success.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'Storage repair against a live backup'. The older snapshot's manifest is re-written (through Write-Manifest, witness valid) with a raw object's row flagged Compressed=Yes, a repairable finding (precondition asserted). With a child backup parked in the no-marker window, Repair-BackupStorageForm throws [SR-075/lock-held], logs it through the caller's logger, and the SHA-256 of every file under BackupPath and ChangePath is unchanged; once the child is killed the same repair repairs the finding. MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-10-09: with the repair skipping the lock it rewrote the snapshot manifest under the live backup, failing the single byte assertion StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1:856 (and the token and log assertions).

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'Kit refresh against a live backup'. The older snapshot's RECONSTRUCT.ps1 is made to differ from the root's (precondition asserted). With a child backup parked in the no-marker window, Update-BackupSnapshotKit throws [SR-075/lock-held], logs it, and every byte under BackupPath and ChangePath is unchanged; once the child is killed the same refresh makes the snapshot kit equal the root's. MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-10-09: with the refresh skipping the lock it overwrote the snapshot kit under the live backup, failing the single byte assertion StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1:909 (and the token and log assertions).

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe '-Action Verify through the entry point with the lock held'. The real FileBackup.ps1 runs in a child process with -ExitCode while the test process holds the store's OS lock: a read-only Verify exits 0; -RepairStorage and -RefreshKits each exit 4 (retry later; 2 until 2026-10-27) with [SR-075/lock-held] in their output; every byte under BackupPath and ChangePath is unchanged across all three.

tests/Unit/StagingOsLock.Tests.ps1 Describe 'The maintenance lock edge cases and placement'. Under -WhatIf both mutators run while the lock is held (no lock taken); a repair given no change root throws [SR-075/lock-held]; a repair given a change root that does not exist creates it, takes the lock there and leaves it free afterwards. From the engine AST, Enter-StoreMutationLock is called exactly once in each mutator and before its first audit, enumeration or mutating command.

tests/Unit/Coverage.Tests.ps1 Describe 'Prune and the pool check read one manifest at a time' (plan C43), on the three-run prune timeline. (a) Read-Manifest seen through a spy: Get-SnapshotPrunePlan reads no folder's manifest more than twice, the plan has no Manifests member, the index records carry no Manifest, and each item names a destination row by position whose RelativePath and content key match. (b) The destination manifest is rewritten with its rows reversed after planning; Publish-PruneManifest throws and the manifest is byte-identical. (c) An empty file planted at the destination name of the endangered object; the plan still lists the key and Remove-BackupSnapshot refuses. (d) keep.txt's only object emptied in the backup root; Test-PoolResolves. Expected outcome: (a) one manifest at a time, positions correct. (b) 'changed after the prune was planned', nothing written. (c) Refused, code 2, one destination-collision refusal; the target's good copy is still there with its original hash (before C43 the damaged copy counted as supply and the good copy was deleted). (d) one broken-pool problem for the backup root's keep.txt row, its message saying damaged.
